description: The National Geotechnical Properties Database of the British Geological Survey stores ground investigation data from commercial site investigations carried out for civil engineering. The catalogue entry and BGS page read on 2026-09-28 describe more than 450,000 laboratory test samples and core descriptions, borehole observations and in-situ tests from over 96,000 boreholes taken from more than 4,800 site investigation reports, covering borehole details, lithology, field and laboratory geotechnical tests and environmental chemistry. Much of it comes from trunk road construction schemes supplied by Highways England and other major projects, entered from AGS transfer files or by hand from paper reports, and BGS offers an AGS validation tool for deposits and downloadable property reports for key formations such as the Mercia Mudstone and Lambeth Group. Coverage is Great Britain, clustered along major infrastructure corridors. Access is on request: the database serves BGS enquiries and external customers, and no licence or cost is published on the pages read. Caveats: the spread follows where projects were built, and older records were keyed from paper. It supports geohazard and resilience studies, such as characterising soils along a road or rail corridor for slope stability or seismic site response. Related records: BGS scanned site investigation records and Geological Survey Ireland's geotechnical data.
